extraction.name: NeedleBench
extraction.description: A comprehensive synthetic framework designed to assess retrieval and reasoning performance in bilingual long-context tasks with adaptive context lengths. Tasks are categorized into information-sparse scenarios (minimal relevant details in extensive irrelevant text) and information-dense scenarios (Ancestral Trace Challenge with relevant information continuously distributed throughout context).
extraction.creator: Mo Li, Songyang Zhang, Taolin Zhang, Haodong Duan, Yunxin Liu, Kai Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: NeedleBench tasks are constructed using synthetic, abstract, and fictional statements or relational facts deliberately designed to avoid overlap with real-world knowledge or pretraining data. For information-sparse tasks, the haystack for English tasks is built by extending prompts with passages from the PaulGrahamEssays dataset, and for Chinese tasks, the ChineseDomainModelingEval dataset is used. The Ancestral Trace Challenge (ATC) is programmatically constructed with randomized names and diverse relationships to ensure every sentence contains critical information.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: For information-sparse tasks, raw data consists of passages from the PaulGrahamEssays dataset for English and the ChineseDomainModelingEval dataset for Chinese, which serve as filler content. The needles are synthetic, abstract, and fictional statements or relational facts. For the ATC task, all content is programmatically generated with randomized names and diverse kinship relationships.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manual annotation of approximately 10% of observed errors from the ATC task, focusing on cases where the question type is 'identifying the eldest ancestor'. Error types were categorized and representative examples were provided.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Error analysis identified main error types including under-thinking (60.2%), partial understanding error (12.9%), instruction following error (7.5%), repetitive output (7.5%), hallucination error (7.5%), and other errors (4.5%). Representative prompt and response examples were provided for each error category.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Keyword-aware scoring approach using GPT-4 tokenizer for measuring token lengths. Automated evaluation using exact match (EM) metric based on model's ability to output correct answer in required format \boxed{...}
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark uses synthetic, abstract, and fictional statements deliberately designed to avoid overlap with real-world knowledge or pretraining data. Tasks are bilingual (English and Chinese), with performance gaps observed between languages, where English results are typically higher than Chinese across most models.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: NeedleBench is a synthetic benchmark and may not fully reflect the complexity of real-world tasks. The benchmark focuses on specific retrieval and reasoning capabilities and may not capture all aspects of long-context understanding. Token lengths are measured using the GPT-4 tokenizer, which may introduce measurement discrepancies across different models.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset uses synthetic names and relationships (e.g., kinship relationships, parent-child, ancestor-descendant) but these are fictional and randomly generated to avoid real personal information.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: NeedleBench is designed for evaluating and testing large language models' long-context retrieval and reasoning capabilities across varying information densities. It supports evaluation at flexible context lengths (4k, 8k, 32k, 128k, 200k, 1000k, and beyond) and includes both information-sparse tasks (retrieval) and information-dense tasks (complex reasoning).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: All codes and resources are publicly available at OpenCompass. All reproducible scripts, code, and datasets will be made available upon publication.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Tasks are categorized into information-sparse and information-dense scenarios. Information-sparse tasks insert synthetic needles (key information units) at varying depths within filler content. Information-dense tasks (ATC) embed relevant information continuously throughout context with varying needle counts (2 to 512) to increase logical complexity and context length. Needles are strategically inserted at various positions to test retrieval and reasoning across different context lengths (4k, 8k, 32k, 128k, 200k, 1000k).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Synthetic, abstract, and fictional needles (key information units) are constructed to avoid overlap with real-world knowledge or pretraining data. For English tasks, haystack (filler content) is built using passages from PaulGrahamEssays dataset. For Chinese tasks, ChineseDomainModelingEval dataset is used. Token lengths are measured using GPT-4 tokenizer. A buffer is subtracted from target context length to mitigate instruction truncation risk across different tokenizers.

name.evidence: we introduce NeedleBench, a comprehensive synthetic framework designed to assess retrieval and reasoning performance in bilingual long-context tasks

description.evidence: we introduce NeedleBench, a comprehensive synthetic framework designed to assess retrieval and reasoning performance in bilingual long-context tasks with adaptive context lengths (e.g., 32k, 128k, and beyond). NeedleBench systematically embeds key data points at varying depths to rigorously test models' capabilities in diverse settings. Tasks within NeedleBench are categorized into two distinct scenarios: information-sparse, characterized by minimal relevant details embedded within extensive irrelevant text to simulate simpler real-world retrieval tasks; and information-dense, implemented as the Ancestral Trace Challenge
